newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia ends monopoly in exports insurance.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia ends monopoly in exports insurance.

text.p: The Tunisian parliament passed a law on Tuesday ending the state's monopoly in insurance of exports.

Under the new law, all the country's insurance companies will be allowed to insure exports along with state-controlled Compagnie Tunisienne d'Assurance et du Commerce exterieur (COTUNACE) which, so far, was the only one allowed to do so.

Offshore firms working in Tunisia were allowed to insure their exports with resident insurance companies. They were not authorised under the previous legislation. There are more than 800 off-shore firms in Tunisia, working mainly in the textiles sector.
Exporters will also be allowed to have an option to insure trade or political risks or both depending on their needs, which was not the case in the past.

Among other advantages of the new law was the fact that exporters inside the country will be able to deal with local branches of insurance companies and that it establishes competition on the market, a parliament report said.
Value of Tunisian exports between 1985 and 1995 amounted to 2.663 billion dinars or 8.0 percent of the total exports, the report said.

Tunisia has 15 insurance companies, COFACE excluded. Nine of them are privately-owned and hold nearly 44 percent of market share, two are controlled by the state, and four are mutual societies. The market has also seven offshore branches of foreign insurance firms.
COFACE says that some 14 percent of resident exporters had been subscribing to an insurance contract with it.
The new law also established a fund which will be in charge of re-insuring non-commercial exports risks or commercial risks for some goods seen as of essential interest for the Tunisian economy.
The Tunisian government last year asked the country's insurance industry to prepare for an opening up of the market to foreign firms by 1999.
